Add a licence-name gate with an allowlist (#287)

Add tools/check-licence-names.py, its allowlist
tools/licence-names-allowlist.tsv and its tests
tools/test-check-licence-names.py. The gate lists the tracked files with
git ls-files --stage -z, run with a fixed argument list and no shell,
reads each from the work tree as bytes, splits it at line feeds only,
and finds each line that holds 1 of its 3 search terms in any ASCII
letter case; its docstring names the terms. Git gets the gate's
environment without GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_COMMON_DIR, the 3
settings that would point it at another repository or index than the one
it finds at the root. The gate fails on a matching line that no row of
its path claims (unclaimed); on a matching line that holds the markers
of 2 or more well-formed rows of its path (ambiguous), which none of
those rows claims, so a broad marker cannot quietly take lines of
another kind; on a well-formed row whose claimed lines differ in number
from its count (stale), fewer or more, which includes a row whose lines
are gone, though a row of a path that cannot be read is not reported
stale, since its lines are unknown; and on a malformed row, which claims
nothing and whose marker makes no line ambiguous: a row with a number of
fields other than 4, a carriage return, a count that is not canonical
ASCII decimal, an owner other than unit-2, unit-3 or keep, an empty
marker, a path that is not tracked, a path of a named exception, or the
path and marker of an earlier row that has 4 fields and no carriage
return, whether or not that earlier row is well formed. It compares a
count as text, so a wrong count of any length gives a named problem. The
gate fails closed, exiting 1 and naming the cause, and turns no error
into an empty or clean result: when the system has no O_NOFOLLOW or the
root cannot be opened as a folder, and then it runs no git and reads no
file; when git ls-files cannot run, fails or lists nothing; when it
gives an entry that cannot be read (one with no tab, or without exactly
3 fields before its tab); when an entry is unmerged (a stage other than
0); when a tracked path has a mode other than 100644 or 100755, such as
a symbolic link (120000) or a submodule (160000); when a tracked path is
not a regular file in the work tree (which includes a path that is
absolute, a path with a part that is empty, 1 dot or 2 dots, and a path
with a parent at any depth that is a symbolic link or anything else but
a folder) or cannot be opened or read; when a folder or the file that
the gate opened for a tracked path is no longer in its place after the
read; and when the allowlist cannot be read or is not UTF-8. When git
ls-files lists entries and the gate can read none of them, it names each
entry and no other cause. The work tree is the root folder as the gate
opens it, once, before git runs. Git starts in that open folder, and
every read of a tracked file, the allowlist included, starts from its
descriptor: each tracked path is opened 1 part at a time, each part
inside the folder opened before it and none through a symbolic link
(O_NOFOLLOW, which the system applies at each open). So neither a
symbolic link in the work tree, made before or during the run, nor a
root replaced after the open can lead a read outside it, and while no
other process moves a folder or file of the work tree, each read is of
the entry at its tracked path in the work tree. The gate does not
prevent a read outside the work tree by a process that moves a folder or
file that the gate opened out of it during the run: an opened folder or
file is read wherever it is moved, and a process that can move it can as
well put any bytes at the tracked paths. After the read the gate checks
that each folder and the file that it opened is still in its place, the
entry at its name in the folder before it, and refuses the bytes that it
read when one is not. The cases that remain are in the list below. On a
system without O_NOFOLLOW the gate refuses to run, since without it no
path can be opened without following a symbolic link. The root and each
folder and file below it are opened without waiting (O_NONBLOCK), so a
FIFO in the place of any of them is refused, with or without
O_DIRECTORY, and not waited on. File content is data: no line of a file
is run, parsed as code or printed whole. It makes git's message and an
error's text 1 line and cuts them to 300 characters; then, in each field
that it shows, it writes a backslash and each character outside
printable ASCII once as a backslash escape. Its own 3 files are its
named exceptions; each must be tracked and must hold a matching line.
The allowlist has 1 row per kind of line in a file: path, count, owner
and a literal marker. The gate refuses an owner other than unit-2,
unit-3 or keep; whether a row's owner is the right one is reviewed, and
the gate does not check it.

The gate's docstring states what it does not cover. Not covered:
another spelling of a licence, such as one in words without the 3
terms, a term split over 2 lines or a lookalike character outside
ASCII; untracked and ignored files; the index copy of a file whose
work-tree copy differs (in CI they are equal); a folder or file of the
work tree that is a mount point, such as a bind mount over a tracked
file, and a file that is a hard link, each read where it stands; a
folder or file that another process moves out of the work tree after
the gate opens it, whose bytes the gate reads
wherever it is, and refuses only when that folder or file is not back
in its place at the check after the read, since that check sees only
where it is then; the reads of git ls-files, of the repository that
git finds from the open root folder, its index and its configuration,
which can lie outside the work tree; whether a line is a true
statement of a licence; whether the owner of a row is right, which is
reviewed prose; and the named exceptions' own lines. A row counts
lines per file, so fixing 1 line and adding another of the same kind
in the same file passes.

The tests build throwaway git repositories and run the gate with no
setting of git taken from the caller's environment or configuration.
Each refusal case that runs the gate first runs it on the unchanged
repository, which must pass, then makes the change that it tests, to the
repository, to the gate's PATH or, through a launcher, to the gate's
process, in 1 or more steps, such as tracking a file and then deleting
it from the work tree. It then requires exit 1, exactly 1 summary line
on standard output (for --list, only path:count lines and then a total
line), and problem lines that match, 1 for 1, the cause and any
consequence that the case names with its reason, with none left over.
Where a cause is also the start of the line of another cause, or a line
must show no text of a file, the problem lines are compared whole. Each
subtest makes its change to the unchanged repository. The helper that
checks a refusal fails the case when no run of the gate passed earlier
in that case on the repository as it was built. No run of the gate may
write a character outside printable ASCII. 1 case requires the gate to
escape a tracked path that holds an escape byte, a backslash, DEL and
characters outside ASCII in the problem lines for a file deleted from
the work tree, a tracked symbolic link, a parent that is a file, an
unmerged entry, a line that holds the markers of 2 rows, and a stale
row. 1 case pins the rule of the helper that checks a refusal: the
helper must fail when no run of the gate passed before it, when the only
run that passed was on a changed index, and when the only run that
passed was on changed bytes of a tracked file, and must check the
refusal after a run that passed on the repository as it was built. 10
cases call the gate's file reader in a separate python3 -I process that
loads the gate by file path: 1 reads a regular file as a control; 6
replace os.lstat or os.fdopen in that process alone to reach an open
descriptor that is not a regular file, a symbolic link that appears
after the lstat check, a symbolic link to a folder outside the work
tree, a file and a FIFO, each in place of a parent after the lstat
check, and a read error, once with the system's text and once with a
text of whitespace, characters outside printable ASCII, a backslash and
more than 300 characters; 1 replaces os.open to move a folder at depth
1, a folder at depth 2, the folder at depth 1 that holds it, a file, and
a folder at depth 1 whose name holds an escape byte, a backslash, DEL
and characters outside ASCII out of the work tree, each just after the
gate opens it, and then replaces os.fdopen to make each of those moves
while the gate reads the file; 1 makes the same moves just after the
gate opens each entry and then puts in the place of the moved entry a
new entry of the same kind, and then a symbolic link to the moved entry;
and 1 removes os.O_NOFOLLOW, once with README.md and once with a path
that holds those characters. 9 cases give the gate a stand-in git, a
Python script alone on its PATH: 1 exits 3 with a message like that
text; 1 lists the repository's 4 files and paths that are not plain
relative, 1 of them leading out of the work tree, to the gate and to
--list; 1 lists the repository's 4 files and, before it exits, replaces
the root with a symbolic link to a copy whose allowlist holds a
malformed row and records its working folder, to the gate and to --list;
1 lists the repository's 4 files and records the folder that it starts
in, after a launcher has replaced the root in the same way, to the gate
and to --list; 1 lists the repository's 4 files, an entry whose mode and
an entry whose stage each hold an escape byte, a backslash and a byte
outside ASCII, to the gate and to --list; and 4 list 3 entries that
cannot be read, 1 with no tab, 1 with 2 fields before its tab and 1 with
4, to the gate and to --list, 2 beside the repository's 4 files and 2
alone. 1 case runs the gate through a python3 -I launcher that first
removes os.O_NOFOLLOW, to the gate and to --list. 4 cases run the gate
through another python3 -I launcher that changes the gate's process
alone, each to the gate and to --list: 1 replaces the root after the
gate opens it and before git starts, in the stand-in case above; 1 moves
a folder at depth 1, the folder at depth 1 above a folder at depth 2 and
a file out of the work tree, each just after the gate opens it and again
while the gate reads the file; 1 removes os.O_DIRECTORY, with a file and
then a FIFO as the root; and 1 makes the change into the root folder
fail before git starts, as on a root folder of mode 0600 that the gate
can open and git cannot enter. 1 case loads the test file in a python3
-I process whose PATH is a relative folder that holds git, and requires
the git that it finds to be an absolute path. 3 cases read no repository
and run no gate. They require each block that a row of BLOCKS in the
tests names to be word for word the same in each text that states it:
the gate's docstring, the test docstring and the squash message, as the
row names them, and, in an export for review, the description and
SQUASH-MSG, which state every block. They compare no other text, and
they require SQUASH-MSG to equal .github/squash/287.txt; a text that is
not there is skipped, and the skip names it.

The Agent Plugins manifest workflow runs the tests and the gate as 2
new steps, and tools/run_all_checks.sh runs them as 2 new run lines.
tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the new digest of that script.
.github/squash/287.txt holds this message.

Checks a reviewer can rerun from the repository root, with their
expected outcomes:

    python3 -I tools/check-licence-names.py

exits 0, and at the head of this change its last line is
"check-licence-names: checked: 59 lines in 35 files; 0 problem(s)".

    python3 -I tools/check-licence-names.py --list

exits 0 and prints 1 line of path and count per file, then the line
"total: 59 lines in 35 files".

    python3 -I tools/test-check-licence-names.py
    python3 -I tools/test-run-all-checks.py

each exit 0.
